title: Towers
statement:
You are given 'N' cubes in an array 'ARR' in a certain order, and your task is to build towers using them.

Whenever two cubes are on top of each other, the upper cube must be smaller than the lower cube.

You must process the cubes in the given order. You can always either place the cube on top of an existing tower or begin a new tower. What is the minimum possible number of towers?

For example: given N = 3, ARR[] = 3, 2, 1. The answer will be one because you can stack one over two over 3.
inputFormat:
The first line contains T, the number of test cases.
For each test case:
The first line contains N, the number of cubes.
The second line contains N space-separated integers, the array ARR.
outputFormat: For each test case print the minimum number of towers.

sampleCases.explanation: First test case: cubes 3, 2, 1 can all be stacked into a single tower because each cube is strictly smaller than the one below it. Second test case: cubes 1, 2, 3 are in ascending order, so each requires a new tower, giving 3 towers.
In the first test case, the cubes can be placed into 2 towers: [9, 8, 7, 6] and [7]. In the second test case, 3 towers are formed.
